title: Resilient k-Clustering

problem.claim: Design clustering algorithms that preserve clustering structure and return high-quality solutions when input points are perturbed.

gap.claim: Classic clustering algorithms have weak resiliency guarantees.

contributions.claim: Introduces a formal notion of algorithmic resiliency for clustering, requiring similar outputs on close inputs.
Develops new algorithms for k-center, k-median, and k-means with improved resiliency guarantees.
Provides an experimental analysis of the techniques on real-world instances.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that classic algorithms have weak resiliency guarantees.
The authors report experimental effectiveness of their techniques on real-world instances.

narrative_sequence.summary: Studies resilient clustering under perturbations of input points.
Introduces a formal definition of algorithmic resiliency for clustering.
Develops algorithms for k-center, k-median, and k-means after identifying weak resiliency in classic algorithms.
Reports experimental analysis on real-world instances.

source_observation.claim: Similar outputs on close inputs are used as the rough requirement for algorithmic resiliency.

interpretation.claim: Robust clustering can be framed as stability of algorithm outputs under small input changes.

application.claim: When designing clustering methods for perturbed data, evaluate both solution quality and output stability.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the perturbation model or conditions under which output similarity is required.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the perturbation metric, scale, or formal resiliency guarantees.
It omits algorithmic details, approximation bounds, and proof information.
The experimental datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are not provided.
